results.screen:
You press the letter into Tam's palm. His fingers close over it and feel along the folds until they find the wax, and he turns the paper over once, slowly, the way a man weighs a stone. He holds it a little away from his face, though his milk-white eyes take in nothing of it, and his mouth tightens. "I can't read it, friend," he says. "Not the seal, and not the hand under it. The river fever took my sight before it took anything else, and no amount of asking brings it back." He lays the letter flat across his knee. The ferry drifts on the black water, and the far bank is still only a dark line. Tam's thumb runs the edge of the wax, slow and careful, as if the shape might tell him something after all. "Whose mark is it?" he asks, and turns his face toward you, waiting.
